summary: Branch-resolved Pauli-block spectroscopy estimates the signed per-cycle residual $ZZ$-rotation angle $\vartheta_c$ in two-qubit gates by measuring the closed four-moment block $\{IX, IY, ZX, ZY\}$ and forming differential branch coherences $C_\pm$ conditioned on the control qubit. On a QuantumCTek cloud processor (66 transmons with tunable couplers), the echoed protocol achieves near-unit-slope injection response and one-step point-estimate feedback suppression ($|\vartheta_c|_{R0}/|\vartheta_c|_{R1} \approx 16$) while preserving branch contrast $\min|C| \gtrsim 0.83$.
motivation: Standard fidelity benchmarks and randomized benchmarking are quadratically insensitive to small coherent residual phases and carry no sign information; repeated Ramsey amplification cannot reliably disentangle the nonlocal $ZZ$ deviation from ordinary target-qubit detuning $\beta_c$, SPAM errors, and contrast loss in long sequences.
method: The protocol repeats a calibrated residual cycle $N$ times on probe $|+\rangle|+\rangle$, measures the four Pauli moments via two target pre-rotation bases ($X$ and $Y$), forms complex branch coherences $C_\sigma(N) = (r_{IX} + ir_{IY}) + \sigma(r_{ZX} + ir_{ZY})$ with $\sigma=\pm1$ labels, and extracts the differential phase slope via matrix-pencil pole fitting: $\vartheta_c$ splits the two branch slopes in opposite directions while $\beta_c$ shifts them together. An optional echoed variant $(XX)U_{\mathrm{cyc}}(XX)U_{\mathrm{cyc}}$ suppresses removable local $IZ$ terms while preserving $ZZ$.
result: Numerical simulations with injected $\vartheta_c$, detuning, damping ($\Gamma = 10^{-3}$ cycle$^{-1}$), and SPAM confirm unbiased signed readout down to $|\vartheta_c| = 10^{-3}$ rad/cycle and distinguish opposite-sign errors at equal infidelity; on native CZ pulses, injection gain $G_{\mathrm{inj}} \approx 57.1$ rad/(detune unit) gives linearity slope $1.10$ ($R^2 = 0.996$), and one feedback step yields $16\times$ suppression of native residual with branch contrast preserved.
